transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

Probably not faulty. On Beko induction hobs, a flashing “U” usually means the hob can’t detect a suitable pan on that cooking zone.

Induction needs cookware with a magnetic, flat base. A saucepan that works on gas or ceramic may not work on induction.

Try this:

• Test the pan with a fridge magnet on its base. If it doesn’t stick firmly, it won’t work.
• Make sure the pan is centred on the marked cooking zone and is not too small for it.
• Check the base is flat and clean — warped, very thin, aluminium, copper, glass, or some stainless-steel pans won’t be recognised.
• If you have one, try a pan labelled “induction suitable” or with the induction coil symbol on the bottom.

If an induction-compatible pan gives the flashing U on every zone, then it could be an installation or appliance fault and is worth reporting to the fitter/retailer while it’s new. But in most cases, the U is simply the hob rejecting the saucepan rather than a fault with the hob.

I tried the magnet! It doesn't stick to my saucepans, but it does stick to my cast-iron casserole, and that one did heat. The pans are definitely centred on the zone. So do I just have to buy all new pans?!

Yes — for induction, you’ll need pans with a magnetic (ferrous) base. Since your cast-iron casserole heats, the hob is working normally.

You do not necessarily need to replace everything straight away:

• Keep using the cast iron where practical.
• Buy a few essential induction-compatible pans first, such as a small saucepan, larger saucepan and frying pan.
• Look for pans marked “suitable for induction” or the induction-coil symbol (a row of loops).
• A magnet should stick firmly to the bottom of the pan — that’s a useful quick check in a shop.

Your existing pans are likely aluminium, copper, or non-magnetic stainless steel. They generally won’t work directly on induction.

There are induction adaptor/converter discs that sit between the hob and a non-induction pan, but they are slower, less efficient, can get extremely hot, and may not be recommended by Beko for your model. In practice, buying induction-ready cookware is usually the better option.
